chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa b. Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali b. Abi Hamza, from Yahya b. Abi Ishaq, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, peace be upon them.

He said: The Prophet (s) was asked: Where were you when Adam was in Paradise? He said: I was in his loins. He descended to the Earth with me in his loins. I boarded the Ark in the loins of my father Nuh. I was thrown into the Fire in the loins of my father Ibrahim. None of my ancestors ever committed adultery. God, the Mighty and Majestic, did not cease transferring me from pure loins to purified wombs, guiding and guided, until God took my pledge in prophethood and my covenant in Islam. He clarified every one of my characteristics, and He established my mention in the Torah and the Gospel. He raised me to His heaven and derived for me a name from His most beautiful names — my nation are the praisers, the Possessor of the Throne is Mahmud (the Praised), and I am Muhammad.

key_terms.أسماء الحسنى: the Most Beautiful Names; the divine names and attributes of God
key_terms.الحمادون: the praisers; those who excessively praise God, related to the root h-m-d
key_terms.سفاح: adultery or fornication; illicit sexual union outside of marriage
key_terms.صلب: loins; the backbone/lineage through which prophetic light was transmitted from father to son

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about his existence before his birth and the purity of his lineage?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition from the assembly gatherings of Shaykh al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (s) responds to a question about his pre-earthly existence by describing how his spiritual light was transmitted through the pure lineage of prophets — from Adam through Nuh and Ibrahim — emphasizing that none of his ancestors committed adultery. The hadith concludes with the profound etymological connection between the Prophet's name Muhammad and God's name Mahmud, both deriving from the root h-m-d (praise), with his nation being called 'the praisers.' This teaching was understood by its audience as establishing the Prophet's primordial nobility and the divine plan behind his lineage.
